question: What will be the US unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted, BLS) for September 2026, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of the US unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted, BLS) for September 2026 (FRED series UNRATE). Later revisions are ignored.
baseline:
Computed by code from FRED UNRATE (Unemployment Rate, Percent, frequency M): latest observation 4.1000 for 2026-08-01.
The target period 2026-09-01 is 1 observation(s) ahead. Percentiles for the target period from the

p5: 3.8, p10: 3.9, p25: 4.0, p50: 4.1, p75: 4.2, p90: 4.3, p95: 4.3

research:
I couldn't open BLS, FRED, Trading Economics or Kalshi pages directly because fetches were refused, so the figures below come from search snippets. I left out everything published after 2026-09-11.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on FRED UNRATE (BLS CPS, seasonally adjusted), using the first value published. The September 2026 figure is due in the Employment Situation release scheduled for 2026-10-02 at 8:30 ET. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.htm)
- 2026-09-04: The latest published value was 4.1% for August 2026, the same as July. The code-supplied FRED baseline agrees (4.1 for 2026-08-01). [TrendForce](https://datatrack.trendforce.com/blog/content/63698/us-august-unemployment-rate-remains-flat-at-41-surge-in-nonfarm-payrolls-reverses-weak-expectations)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The September CPS reference week includes 2026-09-12, and the figure won't be published until 2026-10-02.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-10: Initial jobless claims for the week ending Sept 5 were 206,000, unchanged for a second week. The 4-week average was about 206k, so layoffs remain low. [TrendForce](https://datatrack.trendforce.com/blog/content/63997/us-early-september-initial-jobless-claims-flat-for-second-consecutive-week-at-206000-labor-market-maintains-low-layoff-environment)
- Mid-July 2026: Claims bottomed at 189,000, described as the lowest since 1969. Claims have stayed below 220k all year. [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/initial-jobless-claims-remain-near-57-year-lows-continuing-claims-a-3-year-low)
- 2026-09-04: The August report:
  - Payrolls rose 162k against a consensus of about 53-56k, and June-July were revised up by a combined 55k.
  - Unemployment held at 4.1%.
  - The labor force grew by 683k, and participation rose to 61.6% from 61.4%.
  - U-6 fell to 7.7% from 7.9%.
  - Average hourly earnings rose 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y.
  - Commentary said the report raised the odds of a Fed rate hike.
  
  Sources: [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-august-2026), [BabyPips](https://www.babypips.com/news/headline-us-jobs-august-2026-nonfarm-payrolls-beat-forecasts), [FT Portfolios](https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/9/4/nonfarm-payrolls-increased-162,000-in-august), [search summary of Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/unemployment-rate/news/581285)
- Early August 2026: The July report showed unemployment falling to 4.1% from 4.2%. Most of the drop came from people leaving the labor force (down 264k), and participation hit 61.4%, the lowest since early 2021. Payrolls fell 23k, with prior months revised down 103k. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/unemployment-rate/news/573793), [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/us-unemployment-dips-to-4-1-as-labor-force-shrinks-by-264-000)
- A caution from the commentary: the July decline was participation-driven. In August the labor force rebounded and the rate still held at 4.1%.

## 4. Base rates
- The 2026 path:
  - January: 4.3
  - February: 4.4
  - March: 4.3
  - April: 4.3
  - May: 4.3
  - June: 4.2
  - July: 4.1
  - August: 4.1
  
  The trend is gently downward. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/unemployment-rate), [YCharts](https://ycharts.com/indicators/us_unemployment_rate), [TE May](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/unemployment-rate/news/556895)
- The code baseline, built from 1-month changes since 2005, gives:
  - median 4.1
  - p25 to p75: 4.0 to 4.2
  - p10 to p90: 3.9 to 4.3
  - p5 to p95: 3.8 to 4.3
- Typical pattern: in non-recession periods the first-print change is 0.0 about half the time and ±0.1 most of the rest. Moves of ±0.2 or more are uncommon. The CPS standard error on the monthly change is about ±0.2 percentage points (90% confidence).
- Over the past 8 months, the monthly changes ranged from -0.1 to +0.1, and there were no moves of 0.2.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi has a market on September US unemployment (KXU3-26SEP). The only snapshot I found was undated, but its "64 days" countdown suggests it was taken around late July, before the July and August reports. It showed:
  - above 4.1%: 68%
  - above 4.2%: 55%
  - above 4.3%: 45%
  
  These prices are stale, set when unemployment was 4.2-4.3, so they shouldn't be read as current. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxu3/unemployment/kxu3-26sep)
- Kalshi also lists September payroll threshold markets (KXPAYROLLS-26SEP), but the snapshots I saw were thin and old. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/api/public/market/KXPAYROLLS-26SEP-T60000?depth=true)
- I found no published economist consensus for the September unemployment rate dated on or before 2026-09-11. Consensus surveys usually appear in the week before the release.
- The Fed's June 2026 SEP had a median of 4.3% for end-2026 unemployment, above where the rate is now. [Chapman](https://www.chapman.edu/research/institutes-and-centers/anderson-center/_files/current-economic-news-pdfs/2026-current-economic-news/fomc-unemployment.pdf)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-12: The CPS reference week (the week containing the 12th).
- 2026-09-15/16: An FOMC meeting with a new SEP. The commentary around the August report was discussing a possible hike. [Fed SEP page](https://federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcprojtabl20260916.htm)
- Weekly jobless claims on Sept 17 and Sept 24. The Sept 17 release covers the reference week, which makes it the most informative.
- Late September: the Conference Board's labor differential (jobs plentiful versus hard to get).
- 2026-09-30: ADP for September.
- 2026-10-02: The September Employment Situation, which decides the question.
- Key swing factor: participation has been volatile (61.4% in July, 61.6% in August). A reversal in labor force entries could move the rate by ±0.1 regardless of how strong hiring is.
